settings.accounts.signIn.codex: Open a terminal and run Codex with that folder; the browser sign-in opens for the other account.

history.quota.scopeNote: Follows the time range and provider above. Quotas apply to the whole account, regardless of project or model grouping.
history.quota.observedNote: Increases add up changes between recorded samples, excluding reset and plan transitions. Usage between samples cannot be fully reconstructed. Dashed lines mark reset or plan transitions.
history.quota.empty: No quota records in this range. Available quotas are recorded automatically while the app runs.
history.quota.accessible: Quota percentage over time. Exact values and changes are in the table below.
history.modelDetailsNote: Model names and reasoning effort come from local session logs. Original model names are preserved; missing effort is not inferred.
history.quota.guidesNote: Dotted lines mark the warning and critical thresholds; a dashed segment projects the current pace to the reset or to 100 %.
history.quota.cycles.title: Quota cycles
history.quota.cycles.accessible: Peak used percentage of each quota cycle. The same values are in the table below.
history.quota.cycles.perPercentNote: Median over the last {n} complete cycles with full coverage.
history.quota.cycles.partialHint: The app was not sampling the quota near the end of this cycle, so the peak may be too low.
history.quota.cycles.note: Estimate: a cycle starts one window length before its reset deadline and counts the local session-log tokens of that provider in it. Other devices and web usage are not seen, so figures are approximate.

history.roi.incomplete: Some models have no price, so the API-equivalent figure is a lower bound.
history.roi.accessible: Cumulative estimated cost this month against the subscription price.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.export.hint: Writes snapshot.json after every refresh so status bars and scripts can read the numbers. Account e-mails are never included.
integrations.examples.hint: Prints from the snapshot file without starting the app (exit code 2 when it is missing or older than 15 minutes). On Windows, use the full path to the installed program; see docs/STATUSLINE.md.
integrations.pause.hint: Stops the automatic quota requests; local log history keeps updating and Refresh still works. Stays on after a restart.
integrations.backup.title: Backup and restore
integrations.backup.warn: A backup contains local file paths and session metadata (project folders, session sources) from the usage database. It holds no sign-in credentials, but keep it private.
integrations.restore.hint: Pick a backup folder. Nothing changes until you restart; the current data is kept in a pre-restore folder.
integrations.restore.ready: Backup from {date} is ready. Restart to apply it.

settings.preset.power.hint: Every limit as its own ring, percentages inside, refresh every 30 s, notifications on.
settings.preset.screenShare.hint: Masks account e-mails, silences notifications, hides when idle.
settings.preset.cyber.hint: Neon sci-fi surface with percentages in the rings.

privacy.intro: Everything stays on this computer except the requests listed here. There is no telemetry, no analytics and no account.
privacy.item.credentials.title: Sign-in credentials of your CLIs
privacy.item.credentials.detail: Reads the access token that Claude Code (~/.claude/.credentials.json or the macOS Keychain item “Claude Code-credentials”), Codex (~/.codex/auth.json) and, if enabled, Copilot already keep, only to authorise the requests below. The token is never stored by this app, written anywhere or shown, and it is only sent to its own provider.
privacy.item.credentials.control: Providers → Track (a provider that is off is not read)
privacy.item.sessionLogs.title: Session logs
privacy.item.sessionLogs.detail: Reads the token counts and metadata in ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions to build the usage history. Message text is read from the log file only when you open a session in the Sessions tab, and it is never uploaded unless you start an AI assessment (see below).
privacy.item.ownFiles.title: Files this app writes
privacy.item.ownFiles.detail: settings.json and its undo history, the price list and its cache, cached quota readings, and the usage database (token counts, session titles and where each message sits in the log files, not the message text). If you use AI assessment: its settings and saved reports. All of it lives in the config and data folders shown under About.
privacy.item.ownFiles.control: Delete the folders to remove everything
privacy.item.claude.title: Anthropic: Claude quota
privacy.item.claude.detail: api.anthropic.com (usage and profile), authorised with your Claude Code token, at most every 2 minutes. Returns your limits, plan and account e-mail.
privacy.item.claude.control: Providers → Track Claude, Behaviour → Refresh interval
privacy.item.codex.title: OpenAI: Codex quota
privacy.item.codex.detail: chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage, authorised with your Codex token and account id, on the refresh interval. Returns your limits and plan.
privacy.item.codex.control: Providers → Track Codex, Behaviour → Refresh interval
privacy.item.copilot.title: GitHub: Copilot quota (experimental)
privacy.item.copilot.detail: api.github.com/copilot_internal/user, authorised with the github.com token your Copilot editor plugin keeps. Off unless that token was found at the first start. Never verified against a live account.
privacy.item.openrouter.title: OpenRouter: credit balance (experimental)
privacy.item.openrouter.detail: openrouter.ai/api/v1/key (and /credits for an unlimited key), authorised with the API key found in the environment variable you name. Off unless you switch it on. Never verified against a live account.
privacy.item.update.title: GitHub: app update check
privacy.item.update.detail: Reads latest.json from this project’s GitHub releases once a day (the first check about 30 seconds after start) and when you press “Check for app updates”. The download only starts when you click Install.
privacy.item.update.control: Updates → Check for app updates daily
privacy.item.pricing.title: Price list check
privacy.item.pricing.detail: Downloads pricing.json from this project’s GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com), or from your own https URL if you set one, about a minute after start, then daily, and when you press “Check for price list updates”. It only checks; applying a new price list is a separate click.
privacy.item.pricing.control: Updates → Check for price list updates daily, Price list URL
privacy.item.assessment.title: AI assessment of a session
privacy.item.assessment.detail: Only if you switch on content analysis in Sessions and then click Evaluate on one session, and only after you have seen the redacted preview of exactly what is sent. It goes to the endpoint you configured there (default api.openai.com), authorised with the API key from the environment variable you name.
privacy.item.snapshot.title: Snapshot file for other tools
privacy.item.snapshot.detail: When on, writes snapshot.json (quota percentages, reset times and plans; never e-mail addresses) into the app’s data folder after every refresh, so a statusline or bar can read it with `ai-usage-sidebar --print`. Any program running as you can read that file. Turning it off deletes it.
privacy.item.webhook.title: Webhook alerts
privacy.item.webhook.detail: Only when you switch on webhook alerts and enter an https URL: each notification (title, text, provider, window, level, time) is POSTed to that URL, as generic JSON, ntfy or Slack format. Redirects are refused and the URL is never written to the log. Focus mode silences it like the desktop notifications.
settings.backup.hint: The file holds your settings only: no tokens, no usage data. Importing ignores unknown or invalid values.
settings.backup.recent.hint: The last 5 versions from before a change; a quick run of edits (a slider drag, say) counts as one. A restore can itself be undone.
settings.about.diagnosticsHint: Version, system, provider status, settings and the last log lines. No tokens; e-mails are masked and the log is redacted.
notif.title: Notifications
notif.master.hint: Native notifications plus the optional webhook below. Off sends nothing.
notif.threshold: Warn when a limit is crossed
notif.threshold.hint: Once per window, level and cycle, when usage rises past the warning or critical level.
notif.forecast: Warn when on pace to run out early
notif.forecast.hint: Based on the recent rate; only when the forecast is confident.
notif.budget.hint: At 80 % and 100 % of the monthly budget (estimated cost, never a bill). The budget is set in History.
notif.weekly.hint: Monday around 09:00: last week's tokens, estimated cost, busiest day and limits hit.
notif.webhook.hint: https only. The address may hold a secret: it is kept in settings.json and never written to the log.
notif.webhook.problem.not-a-url: This is not a valid web address.
notif.focus.forever: Focus mode is on: every notification, webhook included, is silenced until you turn it off.
notif.focus.until: Focus mode is on until {time}: every notification, webhook included, is silenced.
notif.permission.denied: The system is blocking notifications for this app. Allow them in your operating system's notification settings.
notif.permission.prompt: The system has not yet allowed notifications for this app. Send a test to be asked.
